summary: The module ships a solid RAKP2-hash grabber (SHA1/SHA256) plus a Get Channel Auth Capabilities decoder, but stops short of the definitive cipher-0 proof, never issues Get Channel Cipher Suites (0x54) or Get Device ID (0x01), ignores three auth-status bits it already parses (per-message auth off, user-level auth off, KG set), never attempts HMAC-MD5 RAKP, and never publishes the enumerated existing_users / vendor / GUID back to the shared cred+asset pipeline that other modules would consume.
existing_capabilities: Get Channel Auth Capabilities (App/0x38) UDP probe on channel 0x0E, admin priv
Anonymous logon + null-user bit decode (auth_status bits 0,1)
Cipher-0 heuristic: 'none' auth + IPMI 2.0 (CVE-2013-4786) — reported with caveat
RMCP+ Open Session Request (payload 0x10) with configurable auth alg
RAKP Message 1/2 exchange, HMAC extraction to hashcat -m 7300 / -m 7302 lines
Multi-user + multi-alg RAKP sweep with short-circuit on alg refusal
Username enumeration via RAKP status asymmetry (medium-sev finding)
Cross-service consume: unions BMC-defaults with creds.known_users (AD/BloodHound/SNMP/SMB SAMR)
Per-scan RAKP user cap (25) to bound UDP round-trips

missing_capabilities.name: Get Channel Cipher Suites (App/0x54) — direct cipher-0 enumeration
missing_capabilities.description: Module explicitly punts on this (comment at line 400: 'that's a separate command'). Instead of the current 'none + IPMI 2.0' heuristic, send NetFn App / Cmd 0x54 to channel 0x0E with list-index 0..3 and parse the returned cipher_suite_records. Any record with auth_alg=0x00 is a hard confirm of CVE-2013-4786 (removes 'if cipher suite 0 is actually enabled' hedge from current finding). Also yields the full negotiable list (cipher 1..17), so weak-cipher findings can be precise rather than heuristic.

missing_capabilities.name: Cipher-0 active exploit: complete RMCP+ session with auth_alg=0x00 and issue Chassis Power Status
missing_capabilities.description: Currently only advertises cipher-0. The definitive test is Open Session Request with auth_alg=0 + integrity=0 + confidentiality=0, then RAKP1/RAKP3 with zero-length HMAC, then Set Session Privilege (App/0x3B) admin, then Chassis Status (Chassis/0x01) with the picked username 'admin' and empty password. A successful response is proof-of-exploit — critical finding with kind=ipmi_cipher_zero_proven and payload=power_state. This is the primitive metasploit/ipmitool -C 0 uses and is the single highest-impact IPMI attack.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: IPMI 2.0 spec §13.28 (RMCP+ Open Session), §13.20 (RAKP), §22.18 (Set Session Priv), §28.2 (Chassis Status); Dan Farmer 2013 advisory

missing_capabilities.name: Get Device ID (App/0x01) — vendor/firmware fingerprint pre-session
missing_capabilities.description: Pre-session zero-auth command that returns manufacturer_id (IANA), product_id, device_id, firmware major/minor + aux firmware revision. Enables direct CVE-match: Dell iDRAC 7 <2.30.30.30 (CVE-2018-1000116), HP iLO 4 <2.53 (CVE-2017-12542), Supermicro BMC <3.x (CVE-2013-3623 UPnP+cred), ASPEED AST2400/2500 firmware. Currently the module has ZERO vendor detection — cipher_zero and rakp findings can't be steered per-vendor and CVE mapping is manual.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: IPMI 2.0 spec §20.1 (Table 20-2 Get Device ID response)

missing_capabilities.name: Per-message auth disabled bit surfaced (auth_status bit 4)
missing_capabilities.description: probe() already reads auth_status but only exposes bits 0/1. Bit 4 = 'Per-message Auth Disabled' means once a session opens, individual IPMI messages inside it need no MAC — an on-path attacker can inject arbitrary commands into a legitimate session. Zero-cost to expose; missing today.

missing_capabilities.name: User-level auth disabled bit surfaced (auth_status bit 3)
missing_capabilities.description: Also already-parsed-but-never-emitted. Bit 3 = 'User-level authentication disabled' means IPMI commands at USER privilege can be issued with auth type NONE — sensor reads, event log dump, some vendor extensions with no cred. Info-disclosure at zero cost.

missing_capabilities.name: KG-set bit surfaced (auth_status bit 5)
missing_capabilities.description: auth_status bit 5 indicates the BMC has a non-null KG (BMC key). When KG is NOT set (the default on most rack BMCs), K_uid derivation collapses to HMAC(password) — combined with cipher-0 or captured RAKP2, exploitation is straightforward. Currently ignored.

missing_capabilities.name: HMAC-MD5 (auth_alg=0x02) added to RAKP sweep
missing_capabilities.description: rakp_sweep only iterates SHA1 (0x01) and SHA256 (0x03). Auth alg 0x02 = RAKP-HMAC-MD5 is a valid negotiable algorithm on legacy BMCs (some older Supermicro/Fujitsu). BMCs that offer only MD5 today return zero hashes from recce even though hashcat has mode 7301 (RAKP HMAC-MD5). Missing coverage = missing loot on legacy hardware.

missing_capabilities.name: Default-credential attempt on captured usernames
missing_capabilities.description: Once a user is confirmed by RAKP2 (or username enum), recce should immediately try one round with the vendor's factory default password for THAT username (root:calvin for iDRAC, ADMIN:ADMIN for Supermicro, USERID:PASSW0RD for IBM/Lenovo, admin:admin/Administrator:Administrator generic). Currently the runbook just tells the operator to do it manually. A single successful Set Session Priv + Chassis Status confirms full BMC pwn without waiting for offline crack. Bounded round-trip cost (≤8 users × 1 password = 8 RAKP3 completions).
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Vendor default-cred inventories: Dell iDRAC 6/7/8, HPE iLO 3/4/5, Supermicro X-series, IBM/Lenovo IMM/IMM2

missing_capabilities.name: Get System GUID (App/0x37) — BMC identity
missing_capabilities.description: Pre-session zero-auth command returning the 16-byte BMC GUID. Useful for cross-scan asset dedup (same BMC on multiple management VLANs), and for correlating IPMI with SMBIOS System UUID pulled from Windows via WMI / SMB / SNMP — enabling 'this BMC belongs to that hostname' pivots. Currently the RAKP1 exchange reveals the GUID (server_guid) but recce never surfaces or reports it.

missing_capabilities.name: Get Channel Info (App/0x42) + Get LAN Config Parameters (Transport/0x02)
missing_capabilities.description: Transport/0x02 returns IP source, community string (for PET SNMP traps — often 'public'), destination MAC, VLAN ID, and gratuitous ARP interval. Zero-auth pre-session (session-less request permitted for select parameters). Reveals management VLAN tag → attacker knows which VLAN to hop to for further BMC access; reveals PET SNMP community for cross-service SNMP write.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: IPMI 2.0 spec §23.2 (Get LAN Config Parameters, Table 23-4)

missing_capabilities.name: Get Channel Auth Capabilities on channel 0x01 (LAN #1) not just 0x0E
missing_capabilities.description: Probe uses channel 0x0E (current). Some BMCs expose multiple LAN channels (0x01 primary, 0x02 shared LAN, 0x06 dedicated OOB) with DIFFERENT auth policies — a hardened 'current' channel can hide a lax secondary channel. ipmitool -H … channel authcap 1 4 vs authcap 2 4 vs authcap 6 4 finds these. Currently one-shot on 0x0E only.

missing_capabilities.name: SOL (Serial-Over-LAN) enabled check via Get SOL Config (Transport/0x21)
missing_capabilities.description: If SOL is enabled AND cipher-0/default-creds work → attacker gets a real serial console (BIOS boot, kernel messages, single-user password reset via bootloader). Detecting the SOL-enabled bit lets the finding escalate cipher-0 to include 'and you get console'.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: IPMI 2.0 spec §26.13 (Get SOL Config Parameters, param 1 = SOL Enable)

missing_capabilities.name: Post-auth user-slot enumeration via Get User Access + Get User Name (App/0x44, App/0x46)
missing_capabilities.description: Once cipher-0 or default creds land a session, iterate user IDs 1..15 and dump usernames + privilege levels + enabled bits. Yields ground-truth account inventory (feeds known_users), passwords set/not-set, and reveals hidden admin backdoors (a BMC with root as user 1 + hidden 'service' account at user 15). Currently RAKP status asymmetry gives a best-effort guess.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: IPMI 2.0 spec §22.28 (Get User Access), §22.29 (Get User Name)

missing_capabilities.name: Publish confirmed users back to creds.known_users
missing_capabilities.description: analyze() CONSUMES known_users but never publishes back. rakp_sweep's existing_users (and any user list dumped via App/0x44 post-auth) should be pushed into the shared known-users pipe so downstream modules (SSH, WinRM, LDAP simple bind, HTTP basic on 443, redfish/iLO web) can spray those exact usernames. Today the BMC user 'USERID' or a discovered custom operator account never reaches SSH/WinRM sweeps on the same host.

missing_capabilities.name: Publish vendor tag / firmware version to shared asset pipe → correlate with iDRAC/iLO web ports
missing_capabilities.description: Once Get Device ID identifies iDRAC/iLO/Supermicro, emit a vendor fact for host.ip so http/tls scanners on 443/5900/17988/2381 (iLO web, iLO XML config, iLO chat, iLO Health) know they're facing that same BMC's web UI — and can trigger HP iLO CVE-2017-12542 (auth-bypass via 29 'A's in Connection header) or iDRAC XML config file grab. Currently the vendor tag is nowhere.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: HP SBD SA-2017-004 (iLO 4 CVE-2017-12542); Dell iDRAC XML config export

missing_capabilities.name: Supermicro NVRAM plaintext-password leak on TCP/49152
missing_capabilities.description: Same physical BMC exposes /PSBlock or /IPMIdevicedesc.xml on 49152/tcp returning plaintext admin password. Not on 623/udp but ships-with-the-BMC; when Get Device ID says 'Supermicro' the ipmi module should emit a hint / cross-service fact triggering an http probe on 49152. Widely exploited pre-2014 and still present on unpatched hardware.

missing_capabilities.name: ASF/RMCP Presence Ping fallback discovery (RFC 3621)
missing_capabilities.description: Some BMCs firewall Get Channel Auth Capabilities (dropping RMCP class 7) but still answer ASF class 6 ping (06 00 ff 06 00 00 11 be 80 00 00 00). A ping fallback would flag 'BMC present but auth-cap request dropped' — currently the module returns unreachable and the host is not flagged. Presence-ping response also encodes supported entity type (BMC vs OEM) + IANA enterprise number.

missing_capabilities.name: Wildcard-username BMC detection (username='' returns hash on some Dell iDRAC)
missing_capabilities.description: Certain iDRAC/Sun ILOM firmwares return an HMAC for the empty username '' — the hash is keyed with the anonymous slot's password (often '' or 'anonymous'). rakp_sweep never includes '' as a username, so this class of BMC is missed. One extra request per alg.

missing_capabilities.name: OEM auth type advertisement flagged separately
missing_capabilities.description: 'OEM' auth type in the bitmap (bit 5) usually means an insecure vendor scheme (early HP iLO used a static XOR). Currently lumped into auth_types list with no severity; deserves its own info/medium finding with vendor-specific hint once Device ID is captured.

priority_gaps: Active cipher-0 session completion (Open Session + RAKP1/3 with auth_alg=0, Set Session Priv, Chassis Status) — turn heuristic finding into proof-of-exploit; single most-impactful IPMI attack
Get Channel Cipher Suites (App/0x54) — direct enumeration replaces the 'if cipher-0 is actually enabled' hedge in the current CVE-2013-4786 finding
Get Device ID (App/0x01) pre-session — vendor+firmware fingerprint enables per-BMC CVE match (iDRAC/iLO/Supermicro/ASPEED) and steers cross-service pivots
Surface the three already-parsed but unused auth_status bits: per-message auth disabled (bit 4), user-level auth disabled (bit 3), KG set (bit 5)
Default-credential completion after RAKP2 (root:calvin, ADMIN:ADMIN, USERID:PASSW0RD, admin:admin) — bounded 8 RAKP3 completions confirms pwn without offline crack
HMAC-MD5 (auth_alg=0x02, hashcat -m 7301) added to rakp_sweep — legacy BMCs are currently invisible to hash capture
cross_service_wire_gaps: known_users is CONSUMED but never PUBLISHED: RAKP-confirmed usernames (existing_users) and post-auth user-slot dumps never reach SSH/WinRM/LDAP/HTTP-basic sprayers on the same host

Vendor tag from Get Device ID is not emitted to the shared asset/service pipe — http/tls scanners on 443/17988/2381 (iLO web/chat/XML) never learn they're facing an iLO and don't trigger HP iLO CVE-2017-12542
System GUID (16 bytes) from RAKP1 response is decoded but discarded — cannot dedup a BMC seen on two management VLANs or correlate to SMBIOS System UUID from WMI/SMB
PET SNMP community + management VLAN ID from Get LAN Config are never emitted — SNMP module can't try that community; VLAN-hopping tools can't target the mgmt tag
Supermicro vendor detection would trigger a 49152/tcp NVRAM plaintext-password check (CVE-2013-3623) that today no module attempts
Confirmed BMC IP + MAC would feed the switch-CAM / DHCP correlation pipe so a discovered BMC on 10.x pairs with a hostname in AD
notes: Auth-status bits 3/4/5 are the cheapest win — they are already read into `auth_status` in probe() at line 378, three extra `bool(auth_status & mask)` lines plus three finding blocks and no new network I/O. The Get Channel Cipher Suites (0x54) and Get Device ID (0x01) additions each cost one extra pre-session UDP round-trip and remove the largest hedges from the current findings.
